zh.title: 第一次体验AI脑波英语，家长应该看哪些现场证据？
zh.description: 第一次体验AI脑波英语，不要只听口号。家长应重点看测评记录、进舱前读熟、学习舱训练、出舱检测、错词复现、教练反馈和下一步训练路径。
zh.lead: 第一次体验AI脑波英语，家长最应该看的不是宣传语，而是现场证据：孩子测评记录是否清楚、进舱前是否读熟、出舱后能否复现、错词有没有回收、教练能否讲清下一步。

sections.h2: 为什么第一次体验不能只看“感觉不错”？
paragraphs: 很多家长过去花过不少英语补课费用，最怕的不是再花钱，而是又一次听起来很有道理、回家却没有变化。因此，第一次体验AI脑波英语时，家长不要只看环境、设备和孩子当时的情绪。
更重要的是看现场证据。真正可信的英语训练，应该让家长知道孩子原来卡在哪里、本次训练做了什么、出舱后能否复现、错词如何处理、后续怎么接到听力、阅读、写作和刷卷。
bullets: 不要只听“效果好”，要看记录
不要只看设备，要看教练动作
不要只看当天兴奋，要看复现和错词回收

sections.h2: 证据一：30分钟测评有没有讲清孩子卡点
paragraphs: 测评不是形式。AI脑波英语会先看音标、自然拼读、词汇量、听力反应、阅读卡点、最近考试表现和孩子配合程度。
家长可以重点问一句：我的孩子现在主要卡在什么地方？如果顾问只能笼统说“基础差”，说明还没有把问题拆开；如果能讲清是发音、词汇、阅读速度、听力反应还是考试题型问题，后续训练才有方向。
bullets: 音标和自然拼读是否过关
词汇量差距大不大
听力和阅读到底卡在哪里
孩子是否适合先做3次体验

sections.h2: 证据二：进舱前是不是先读熟、认熟
paragraphs: 如果孩子直接躺进学习舱，家长反而应该追问。AI脑波英语的标准流程是进舱前先把本次词表读熟、认熟、拼写过一遍。
因为词汇要进入听力和阅读，首先要能读准、能识别。进舱前准备越扎实，出舱检测越有意义。
bullets: 是否有本次训练词表
孩子是否跟读并大声朗读
是否做过拼写或自然拼读练习
教练是否确认孩子已经进入可训练状态

sections.h2: 证据三：学习舱训练是不是有明确动作
paragraphs: 学习舱不是“躺着睡一觉”。孩子戴上眼罩和耳机后，要在更安静、更专注的状态里完成节律化输入。
家长可以理解为：听中文想英文，听英文想中文，听拼写时用手空书。学习舱环节的重点，是把单词的声音、拼写和意思反复绑定，而不是让孩子被动听完就结束。
bullets: 眼罩和耳机降低干扰
特定频率声波辅助进入更适合记忆的状态
孩子仍然需要配合完成想词、识别和空书动作
教练需要管理训练节奏

sections.h2: 证据四：出舱检测有没有马上做
paragraphs: 出舱检测是家长最应该看的环节。孩子到底记住了多少，不能靠一句“感觉不错”，要看汉译英、英译汉、拼写和错词记录。
如果一个训练项目没有出舱检测，家长很难判断当天训练是否真的发生了效果。AI脑波英语把出舱检测作为体验课的关键证据，因为它能让家长现场看到孩子是否能复现。
bullets: 汉译英看输出能力
英译汉看识别能力
拼写看准确性
错词本看后续复习重点

sections.h2: 证据五：错词有没有复现和后续安排
paragraphs: 一次体验课不可能解决所有问题。真正重要的是，教练能不能把不稳的词记录下来，并告诉家长下一次如何复现、如何复习、如何逐步接入语法、听力、阅读、写作和刷卷。
这也是AI脑波英语区别于普通试听课的地方：不是听完一节课就结束，而是用记录和复盘决定下一步训练。
bullets: 错词是否被记录
是否安排下次复现
是否说明词汇如何转到听力和阅读
是否给家长明确反馈

sections.h2: 什么样的孩子适合继续系统训练？
paragraphs: 如果孩子愿意配合测评和训练，进舱前能按要求读熟，出舱后能看到复现结果，家长也认可检测和复习机制，就可以进一步评估是否进入系统课程。
如果孩子完全不配合、家长期待“躺一次就满分”、或者不愿意做检测和复习，则不建议直接进入长期训练。AI脑波英语更重视匹配度，而不是把所有孩子都强推到同一套课程里。
bullets: 适合：愿意配合、能接受检测、家长重视过程记录
谨慎：完全抗拒训练、拒绝复习、家长期待不现实

faqs.q: 第一次体验AI脑波英语，家长最应该看什么？
faqs.a: 重点看测评记录、进舱前读熟、学习舱训练动作、出舱检测、错词记录和教练反馈，而不是只看环境或听宣传。
它更适合作为低门槛验证：看孩子是否适合训练、是否愿意配合、出舱后能否复现，以及家长是否认可后续训练路径。

faqs.q: 如果第一次体验效果不错，是否马上报长期课？
faqs.a: 不一定。建议结合测评结果、孩子配合度、出舱检测、错词复现和家庭时间安排，再决定是否进入系统课程。

faqs.q: 如果孩子当天没达到预期怎么办？
faqs.a: 要看原因：可能是音标基础弱、词表难度不匹配、孩子配合度不够，或需要更多复现。教练应基于记录给出调整建议。

zh.cta: 如果孩子英语背了就忘、听力反应慢、阅读看不懂，建议先预约30分钟测评，再通过9.9元3次课观察真实训练证据。

en.title: What Evidence Should Parents Check in a First AI English Learning Cabin Trial?
en.description: A practical checklist for parents and education partners evaluating an AI English learning cabin trial: assessment records, word-list preparation, cabin input, exit testing, error review and next-step recommendations.
en.lead: A first AI English learning cabin trial should not be judged by slogans. Parents and partners should look for observable evidence: assessment records, word-list preparation, cabin-based input, immediate exit testing, error review and a clear next-step plan.

sections.h2: Why should a first trial be judged by evidence, not impressions?
paragraphs: Many families have already spent time and money on English tutoring without seeing meaningful change. That is why a first trial should be evaluated through concrete records rather than excitement or vague promises.

A credible learning process should show where the student started, what was trained, whether the words could be recalled after the session, how errors were captured, and how vocabulary work connects to listening, reading, writing and exam practice.
bullets: Look for records, not slogans
Look for coach actions, not only equipment
Look for recall and error review, not only a good feeling

sections.h2: Evidence 1: Does the assessment explain the real learning gap?
paragraphs: Before the trial, the center should check pronunciation, phonics, vocabulary level, listening response, reading bottlenecks, recent exam performance and student cooperation.
Parents can ask a simple question: where is my child currently stuck? A useful answer should separate pronunciation, vocabulary, reading speed, listening response and exam-skill issues.
bullets: Pronunciation and phonics
Vocabulary recognition and spelling
Listening and reading obstacles
Fit for a short trial

sections.h2: Evidence 2: Was the word list prepared before the cabin session?
paragraphs: A student should not simply lie down and listen. Before entering the cabin, the coach should help the student read, recognize and spell the target word list.
This preparation matters because words that cannot be pronounced or recognized accurately are harder to use in listening and reading tasks.
bullets: A clear word list
Reading aloud with the coach
Spelling or phonics practice
Confirmation that the student is ready for input

sections.h2: Evidence 3: Did the cabin session include active training actions?
paragraphs: The learning cabin is not a passive nap. The student wears an eye mask and headphones to reduce distractions and complete structured rhythmic audio input.
The student is expected to participate: hearing Chinese and recalling English, hearing English and recalling meaning, and using finger-writing during spelling cues.
bullets: Eye mask and headphones reduce distraction
Non-invasive audio input is delivered through headphones
Meaning, sound and spelling are repeatedly linked
The coach manages the session rhythm

sections.h2: Evidence 4: Was exit testing completed immediately?
paragraphs: Exit testing is the most important trust point. Whether the student remembered the words should be checked through Chinese-to-English, English-to-Chinese, spelling and error records.
Without immediate testing, parents and partners have little basis for judging whether the session produced observable learning results.
bullets: Chinese-to-English output
English-to-Chinese recognition
Spelling accuracy
Error list for follow-up review

sections.h2: Evidence 5: Is there an error-review and next-step plan?
paragraphs: One trial cannot solve every English problem. A useful trial should end with a clear explanation of unstable words, review rhythm and the next training path.
For education centers, this evidence also helps evaluate whether the learning cabin model can support parent consultation, delivery quality and conversion.
bullets: Errors are recorded
Review is scheduled
Vocabulary is linked to listening and reading
Parents receive a clear explanation

sections.h2: Who should continue after the first trial?
paragraphs: A student may be a good fit if they cooperate with assessment and training, can follow the coach’s preparation steps, show observable recall after the cabin session, and have a family willing to track review records.
It may be too early to continue if the student refuses all training actions, the family expects a one-session miracle, or no one is willing to follow the testing and review process.
bullets: Good fit: cooperative, testable, willing to review
Use caution: unrealistic expectations, no review, no willingness to be assessed

faqs.q: What should parents check in a first AI English trial?
faqs.a: They should check assessment records, word-list preparation, cabin-based input, exit testing, error records and the coach’s next-step recommendation.

faqs.q: Is a low-cost trial just a marketing hook?
faqs.a: It should be treated as a verification step: whether the student cooperates, whether recall is observable, and whether the family understands the next training path.

faqs.q: Should a family enroll immediately after a good first trial?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. The decision should combine assessment results, cooperation, exit-test performance, review needs and the family’s available training schedule.

faqs.q: Can education centers use the checklist for pilots?
faqs.a: Yes. The same checklist helps an education center evaluate parent consultation, delivery quality and whether the model has repeatable evidence for conversion.

en.cta: Parents can book an assessment before choosing a full program. Education partners can use the same checklist to evaluate whether an AI English learning cabin pilot is suitable for their center.
